requested_by: Helen Marsh, Privacy and Compliance Manager
title: Thirteen privacy and compliance obligations: which are late?
situation: The compliance team is tracking 13 open items as of day 1000: customer requests to see, correct or delete their data, three data breaches, data-retention cases and signed attestations. Some deadlines have already passed, and one customer request was sent to our payroll provider instead of to us. Leadership needs a status report and to know which items must be reported outside the company.
your_task: Apply each item's deadline rule and mark it COMPLIANT, AT_RISK, NON_COMPLIANT or EXEMPT.
Check data-subject requests for identity verification and correct routing between controller and processor.
Check breach notices against the 72-hour regulator deadline and whether affected people were told.
Check retention cases for data kept too long or destroyed too early, allowing for legal holds, and produce the summary report.
why_it_matters: Late breach notices and missed privacy deadlines bring fines, and an expired attestation can cost a customer contract or a license. Acting on a deletion request without verifying identity can hand someone else's data to an impostor.
done_when: All 13 items have a status, a rule and a consequence.
The report shows COMPLIANT 2, AT_RISK 2, NON_COMPLIANT 7, EXEMPT 2, and lists the 4 items needing external reporting.

DSR-5 is routed to the Identity and Access Management (IAM) team to verify the requester's identity before any erasure, and for BR-3 (credential stuffing) affected customers are notified and IAM confirms the compromised accounts were reset.

glossary.DSR (data subject request): A person's request to see, correct or delete the data a company holds about them.
glossary.Data controller: The organization that decides why and how personal data is used.
glossary.Data processor: A company that handles personal data only on the controller's instructions.
glossary.Right to be forgotten: A person's right to have their data deleted, unless a law or legal hold requires keeping it.
glossary.Retention period: The minimum and maximum time a type of record must be kept.
glossary.Attestation: A signed statement that controls are in place, often owed to customers or auditors.
glossary.Credential stuffing: Trying usernames and passwords stolen from other sites on our login page.

talking_point: Tracked 13 privacy and compliance obligations and found 7 non-compliant, including a breach notice 28 hours late, audit logs destroyed 225 days early and an erasure request with no identity verification, with 4 items needing external reporting.
